phase3_findings.description: redacted_refusal_text maps the lock refusal to REDACTED_LOCKING_READ by matching the English substring 'locking reads are not allowed', duplicated as a literal in readonly.py lines 644-645 with no shared constant or error kind; wording drift would silently fall back to REDACTED_READ_ONLY. Extends an existing pattern.

report:
## Verdict: APPROVE with notes (one suggestion, three inconclusive checklist items)
The PR is ready to merge: no reviewer found a defect at or above the important threshold and no checklist item failed; the notes are a suggestion and three items the verifiers could not settle without sqlglot's source.
Rule applied: rule 6 — a finding below the threshold or an INCONCLUSIVE item remains → APPROVE with notes

## Code Review Findings

### 🟡 Suggestion / Minor (1)

<details><summary>1 item</summary>

1. `src/sqllens/safety/rule_sets.py` lines 433-434: `redacted_refusal_text` picks `REDACTED_LOCKING_READ` by matching the English substring `locking reads are not allowed`, duplicated as a literal in `src/sqllens/safety/readonly.py` lines 644-645 with nothing tying them; if the guard's wording drifts the refusal silently falls back to the generic read-only text. Existing pattern this change extends. (raised by 1/6 agents)

</details>

### ℹ️ Informational — Deferred
- VC-1: INCONCLUSIVE (important) — Under the pinned sqlglot and MySQL dialect, every lock clause form (FOR UPDATE/SHARE with OF, NOWAIT, SKIP LOCKED, WAIT n; LOCK IN SHARE MODE) parses to an exp.Lock node reachable by stmt.walk(), including one attached to a Union node [src/sqllens/safety/readonly.py:643]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  The guard at src/sqllens/safety/readonly.py:629-645 walks stmt.walk() and raises on any exp.Lock node; it is correct if sqlglot parses every lock form to exp.Lock reachable by walk(). requirements.txt:103 pins sqlglot==30.31.0. The item has no dependency_sources, and a Glob for **/sqlglot/parser.py under the review directory found nothing, so sqlglot's parser (_parse_locks), exp.Lock and Union's args handling were not readable. The PR's own test (tests/unit/test_safety.py TestLockingReadsRejected, including the Union-attached FOR UPDATE case) asserts the behavior, but I did not run it, and a test is not the library source. Missing evidence: sqlglot 30.31.0 parser.py/expressions.py source, or a run of those tests.

  </details>

- VC-2: INCONCLUSIVE (suggestion) — exp.Lock's 'update' arg is truthy for FOR UPDATE and falsy for FOR SHARE and LOCK IN SHARE MODE, so the message names the strength correctly [src/sqllens/safety/readonly.py:644]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  readonly.py:644 uses sub.args.get('update') to pick 'FOR UPDATE' vs 'FOR SHARE / LOCK IN SHARE MODE'. The claim depends on sqlglot's Parser._parse_locks, but the item has no dependency_sources and the view-head holds no sqlglot source (Grep for 'def _parse_locks' found nothing). Not verified: how _parse_locks sets update= for FOR SHARE and LOCK IN SHARE MODE. Sqlglot copies found elsewhere on the filesystem are outside the supplied sources and were not relied on.

  </details>

- VC-4: INCONCLUSIVE (suggestion) — The comment asserts building the refusal from sub.sql() would copy OF table names and comments into it, and that sqlglot can hang the lock on a Union [src/sqllens/safety/readonly.py:640]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  The comment is at src/sqllens/safety/readonly.py:639-642 and the code at 643-645 checks every exp.Lock node and builds the message from sub.args only, not sub.sql(). Whether sqlglot attaches Lock to a Union, and whether Lock.sql() copies OF tables and comments, depends on installed sqlglot parser and generator behavior. The item has no dependency_sources, sqlglot is not vendored in the head view, and I did not run the parse. The claim is therefore unverified from the views alone. Missing evidence: sqlglot source (parser _parse_lock and set-operation parsing, generator lock_sql) or the output of parse_one('SELECT a FROM t UNION (SELECT a FROM u) FOR UPDATE', read='mysql').

  </details>

- Checklist: 14 passed, 0 failed, 3 inconclusive
- <details><summary>✅ Passed items (14 of 17)</summary>

  - VC-3: The guard message 'locking reads are not allowed' passes through redacted_refusal_text's earlier branches (parse markers, _logged_by_guard, WholeRowSelectError, side-effecting) without matching them and reaches REDACTED_LOCKING_READ [src/sqllens/safety/rule_sets.py:433]
  - VC-5: Doc rule 8 says a lock clause anywhere in the statement is refused, including CTE, derived table, IN subquery and UNION operand, and that the check is only in assert_select_only so read_only=false refuses no lock clause [docs/internal/database-connectors/read-only-safety.md]
  - VC-6: Doc says MySQL read-only row: session does not stop shared-lock reads and only the parser guard's rule 8 keeps them out, and rule-4 SHOW text now refers to deny-walk rules 5-8 [docs/internal/database-connectors/read-only-safety.md]
  - VC-7: The _Inner fake runner and ToolContext.model_construct() / RunSqlToolArgs(sql=...) match the real SqlRunner.run_sql(args, context) signature ReadOnlyGuardRunner calls, and the async test runs under the repo's pytest asyncio config [tests/unit/test_safety.py]
  - VC-8: Changelog says locking reads with any options are refused anywhere in a query before it runs with read_only = true [changelog.d/392.security.md]
  - VC-9: `assert_select_only(sql, dialect="mysql")` raises `UnsafeSqlError` for each of these statements (at minimum): `SELECT a FROM t FOR UPDATE`, `SELECT a FROM t FOR SHARE`, `SELECT a FROM t LOCK IN SHARE MODE`, `SELECT a FROM t FOR UPDATE NOWAIT`, `SELECT a FROM t FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`, `SELECT a FROM t FOR SHARE OF t`, `SELECT a FROM t FOR UPDATE OF t FOR SHARE OF u`, `WITH x AS (SELECT a FROM t FOR UPDATE) SELECT a FROM x`, `SELECT a FROM (SELECT a FROM t FOR SHARE) s`, `SELECT a FROM t WHERE a IN (SELECT a FROM u FOR UPDATE)`, `(SELECT a FROM t) UNION (SELECT a FROM u FOR SHARE)`, `SELECT a FROM t UNION SELECT a FROM u FOR UPDATE` and `SELECT a FROM t UNION (SELECT a FROM u) FOR UPDATE`. [src/sqllens/safety/readonly.py:643]
  - VC-10: Under the MySQL dialect, the `UnsafeSqlError` message for a statement whose only lock clause is exclusive (`SELECT a FROM t FOR UPDATE`) is exactly `locking reads are not allowed (found FOR UPDATE)`, and for one whose only lock clause is shared (`SELECT a FROM t FOR SHARE` and `SELECT a FROM t LOCK IN SHARE MODE`) is exactly `locking reads are not allowed (found FOR SHARE / LOCK IN SHARE MODE)`. For `SELECT a FROM t FOR SHARE OF secret_table /* note */`, the message contains neither `secret_table` nor `note`. [src/sqllens/safety/readonly.py:644]
  - VC-11: `ReadOnlyGuardRunner.run_sql` given `SELECT a FROM t FOR SHARE` under the MySQL dialect raises `UnsafeSqlError` and never calls its inner runner. [tests/unit/test_safety.py]
  - VC-12: `assert_select_only(sql, dialect="mysql")` still accepts `SELECT a FROM t`, `SELECT a FROM t WHERE a IN (SELECT a FROM u)`, `(SELECT a FROM t) UNION (SELECT a FROM u)` and ``SELECT `lock`, `share` FROM `update` `` (which holds the words `lock`, `share` and `update` but no lock clause). [tests/unit/test_safety.py]
  - VC-13: A test pins the sqlglot tree shape the check relies on, under the version `requirements.txt` locks and the MySQL dialect: `SELECT a FROM t FOR UPDATE` parses to one `exp.Lock` node with `update` true, and `SELECT a FROM t FOR SHARE` and `SELECT a FROM t LOCK IN SHARE MODE` each parse to one `exp.Lock` node with `update` false. [tests/unit/test_safety.py]
  - VC-14: `redacted_refusal_text` maps the read-only guard's refusal of a locking read (`refusing to execute non-SELECT SQL: locking reads are not allowed (found FOR UPDATE)`, and the same with `(found FOR SHARE / LOCK IN SHARE MODE)`) to exactly `refusing to execute SQL: locking reads (FOR UPDATE, FOR SHARE, LOCK IN SHARE MODE) are not allowed`, and still maps `refusing to execute non-SELECT SQL: only SELECT (got DELETE)` to `refusing to execute SQL: only a single SELECT query is allowed`. [src/sqllens/safety/rule_sets.py:433]
  - VC-15: `docs/internal/database-connectors/read-only-safety.md` states, in its "What the guard does" rules, that the guard refuses a lock clause (`FOR UPDATE`, `FOR SHARE`, `LOCK IN SHARE MODE`, with any options) anywhere in the statement, and why: MySQL 8.0's read-only session (checked on 8.0.46) refuses `FOR UPDATE` (error 1792) but runs `FOR SHARE` and `LOCK IN SHARE MODE`, whose shared row locks block other sessions' writes until the connection closes. Its MySQL row under "Driver-level read-only enforcement" states that the read-only session does not stop shared-lock reads. [docs/internal/database-connectors/read-only-safety.md]
  - VC-16: `docs/external/configuration.md`'s `read_only` row lists locking reads (`FOR UPDATE`, `FOR SHARE`, `LOCK IN SHARE MODE`) among the statements rejected while `read_only` is true. [docs/external/configuration.md]
  - VC-17: The change adds no lock-clause check outside `assert_select_only`: `assert_no_denied_functions` (the function-denylist check that RLS runs while `read_only = false`) does not refuse `SELECT a FROM t FOR SHARE` under the MySQL dialect. The change also leaves the Tool Errors rules in `src/sqllens/agent/core/system_prompt/default.py` unchanged, so they name no lock refusal, and adds no connector test of how MySQL's read-only session handles locking reads. [tests/unit/test_safety.py]

  </details>
- Reviewed against issue #385 — criteria from the workpad; scope unchanged.

</details>
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] `assert_select_only(sql, dialect="mysql")` raises `UnsafeSqlError` for each of these statements (at minimum): `SELECT a FROM t FOR UPDATE`, `SELECT a FROM t FOR SHARE`, `SELECT a FROM t LOCK IN SHARE MODE`, `SELECT a FROM t FOR UPDATE NOWAIT`, `SELECT a FROM t FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`, `SELECT a FROM t FOR SHARE OF t`, `SELECT a FROM t FOR UPDATE OF t FOR SHARE OF u`, `WITH x AS (SELECT a FROM t FOR UPDATE) SELECT a FROM x`, `SELECT a FROM (SELECT a FROM t FOR SHARE) s`, `SELECT a FROM t WHERE a IN (SELECT a FROM u FOR UPDATE)`, `(SELECT a FROM t) UNION (SELECT a FROM u FOR SHARE)`, `SELECT a FROM t UNION SELECT a FROM u FOR UPDATE` and `SELECT a FROM t UNION (SELECT a FROM u) FOR UPDATE`.
- [ ] Under the MySQL dialect, the `UnsafeSqlError` message for a statement whose only lock clause is exclusive (`SELECT a FROM t FOR UPDATE`) is exactly `locking reads are not allowed (found FOR UPDATE)`, and for one whose only lock clause is shared (`SELECT a FROM t FOR SHARE` and `SELECT a FROM t LOCK IN SHARE MODE`) is exactly `locking reads are not allowed (found FOR SHARE / LOCK IN SHARE MODE)`. For `SELECT a FROM t FOR SHARE OF secret_table /* note */`, the message contains neither `secret_table` nor `note`.
- [ ] `ReadOnlyGuardRunner.run_sql` given `SELECT a FROM t FOR SHARE` under the MySQL dialect raises `UnsafeSqlError` and never calls its inner runner.
- [ ] `assert_select_only(sql, dialect="mysql")` still accepts `SELECT a FROM t`, `SELECT a FROM t WHERE a IN (SELECT a FROM u)`, `(SELECT a FROM t) UNION (SELECT a FROM u)` and ``SELECT `lock`, `share` FROM `update` `` (which holds the words `lock`, `share` and `update` but no lock clause).
- [ ] A test pins the sqlglot tree shape the check relies on, under the version `requirements.txt` locks and the MySQL dialect: `SELECT a FROM t FOR UPDATE` parses to one `exp.Lock` node with `update` true, and `SELECT a FROM t FOR SHARE` and `SELECT a FROM t LOCK IN SHARE MODE` each parse to one `exp.Lock` node with `update` false.
- [ ] `redacted_refusal_text` maps the read-only guard's refusal of a locking read (`refusing to execute non-SELECT SQL: locking reads are not allowed (found FOR UPDATE)`, and the same with `(found FOR SHARE / LOCK IN SHARE MODE)`) to exactly `refusing to execute SQL: locking reads (FOR UPDATE, FOR SHARE, LOCK IN SHARE MODE) are not allowed`, and still maps `refusing to execute non-SELECT SQL: only SELECT (got DELETE)` to `refusing to execute SQL: only a single SELECT query is allowed`.
- [ ] `docs/internal/database-connectors/read-only-safety.md` states, in its "What the guard does" rules, that the guard refuses a lock clause (`FOR UPDATE`, `FOR SHARE`, `LOCK IN SHARE MODE`, with any options) anywhere in the statement, and why: MySQL 8.0's read-only session (checked on 8.0.46) refuses `FOR UPDATE` (error 1792) but runs `FOR SHARE` and `LOCK IN SHARE MODE`, whose shared row locks block other sessions' writes until the connection closes. Its MySQL row under "Driver-level read-only enforcement" states that the read-only session does not stop shared-lock reads.
- [ ] `docs/external/configuration.md`'s `read_only` row lists locking reads (`FOR UPDATE`, `FOR SHARE`, `LOCK IN SHARE MODE`) among the statements rejected while `read_only` is true.
- [ ] The change adds no lock-clause check outside `assert_select_only`: `assert_no_denied_functions` (the function-denylist check that RLS runs while `read_only = false`) does not refuse `SELECT a FROM t FOR SHARE` under the MySQL dialect. The change also leaves the Tool Errors rules in `src/sqllens/agent/core/system_prompt/default.py` unchanged, so they name no lock refusal, and adds no connector test of how MySQL's read-only session handles locking reads.
